title: Genitive 6: After Prepositions (без, у, для, из, от)
description: Five common prepositions (без, у, для, из, от) require the genitive case. Same gender rules apply.
descriptionRussian: Пять предлогов (без, у, для, из, от) требуют родительного падежа. Применяются те же правила по родам.
intro: Until now this case has been about absence. Today absence turns out to have been only one doorway into it, and five extremely ordinary prepositions open the same door. Coffee without milk, a present for my brother, a letter from a friend: none of these are negative, and all of them take the ending you have spent five lessons building. Nothing new to form. A great deal more you can now say.
rules: Five common prepositions take the genitive: без, у, для, из, от. Memorize them as a group.
The noun directly after one of these prepositions follows the same gender rules from Lessons 1 to 3. The trigger changes (preposition instead of нет); the form rules do not.
The preposition is the trigger, not the surrounding sentence. Even in a long sentence, the noun directly after one of these prepositions takes genitive.
examples: Чай без сахара. (Tea without sugar.) сахар → сахара (masculine).
Я из Москвы. (I am from Moscow.) Москва → Москвы (feminine).
Это для мамы. (It's for mom.) мама → мамы (feminine).
Письмо от Антона. (A letter from Anton.) Антон → Антона (masculine animate).
Кофе без молока. (Coffee without milk.) молоко → молока (neuter).

items.hint: After есть, the noun stays in which case?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 5: after есть the noun stays in the nominative. Книга is the dictionary form. Today's lesson moves to a different genitive trigger: prepositions.

items.hint: Без is one of the new genitive-triggering prepositions. Apply Lesson 1's masculine rule.
items.explanation: Без means 'without' and triggers genitive. Сахар is masculine consonant: + -а → сахара. The case rule is the same as for нет; only the trigger changes.

items.hint: Из triggers genitive. Москва is feminine -а.
items.explanation: Из means 'from' or 'out of' and triggers genitive. Москва is feminine -а: -а → -ы → Москвы. Names of places follow the same rules as common nouns.

items.hint: От triggers genitive. Антон is masculine consonant.
items.explanation: От means 'from' (especially from a person or source) and triggers genitive. Антон adds -а → Антона. Compare from-place 'из Москвы' with from-person 'от Антона.'

items.hint: Для triggers genitive. Мама is feminine -а.
items.explanation: Для means 'for' and triggers genitive. Мама is feminine -а → -ы → мамы. The construction 'X для Y' is essential everyday Russian.

items.hint: Молоко is neuter. Apply the neuter rule from Lesson 3.
items.explanation: Молоко is neuter -о → -а → молока. The preposition без triggers genitive across all three genders, just as нет does.

items.hint: Без triggers the genitive. Лимон is masculine consonant.
items.explanation: Без always takes the genitive: без лимона (masculine consonant + -а).

items.promptEnglish: Here is a letter from a friend.
items.hint: От triggers the genitive. Друг is masculine consonant.
items.explanation: От always takes the genitive: от друга (masculine consonant + -а).

items.hint: Из triggers the genitive. Россия ends in -ия.
items.explanation: Из always takes the genitive, and -ия nouns take -ии: Италия → Италии. The same -ия → -ии pattern covers Россия, история, and other -ия nouns.

blanks: Я еду из _____. (I'm coming from the city.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Из triggers genitive. Город is masculine consonant: + -а → города.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это подарок для брат, который любит футбол.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: It's a gift for the brother who loves football.
errorCorrection.explanation: The preposition для always takes the genitive. Брат is masculine consonant, so the genitive adds -а: брата. Брат left as nominative is the most common mistake after для; learners forget the preposition itself selects the case.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я из Россия родом, но сейчас живу в Лондоне.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I'm originally from Russia but currently live in London.
errorCorrection.explanation: The preposition из (from) takes the genitive. Россия ends in -ия, a special soft-stem fem pattern where the genitive ends in -ии: Россия → России. The double -и is the diagnostic ending for -ия nouns.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня письмо от Маша, она пишет каждую неделю.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have a letter from Masha; she writes every week.
errorCorrection.explanation: The preposition от takes the genitive. Маша is feminine ending in -а; the genitive swaps -а → -ы, but the spelling rule after the husher -ш blocks -ы in favor of -и: Маша → Маши. Russian names follow the same case rules as common nouns.

minimalPairs.explanation: Из triggers genitive. Москва is feminine -а → -ы → Москвы. The nominative form Москва would only appear as a subject: 'Москва — большой город' (Moscow is a big city).
Для triggers genitive. Антон is masculine consonant: + -а → Антона. The nominative Антон would appear as a subject: 'Антон работает' (Anton works).

reviewVocab.definition: preposition (a small word like без, для, из, от, у)
reviewVocab.example: Без, для, из, от, у — это предлоги, которые требуют родительного падежа.

reviewVocab.definition: without (preposition; the noun after it takes the genitive)
for (preposition; the noun after it takes the genitive)
